Seven edge cases (thresholds down to 1e-9 and up to 100) also matched on 3 ranks.\n\n**Performance** (4× RTX 3090, times in ms)\n\n| N | original | 1 GPU | 2 GPUs | 4 GPUs |\n|---|---|---|---|---|\n| 1,000 | 7,023 | 7 | 7 | 9 |\n| 2,000 | 88,748 | 10 | 10 | 15 |\n| 30,000 | — | 205 | 144 | 121 |\n| 100,000 | — | 4,561 | 2,416 | 1,346 |\n\nAt 100,000 points, 4 GPUs run 3.4× faster than one. Below roughly 10,000 points, extra GPUs don't help because the fixed cost of each clustering round dominates.\n\n**How it works**\n- **Algorithm:** the result is the same, but the work is far smaller than the original's roughly N⁴ cost:\n  - Each candidate's largest distance to the growing cluster is updated as members are added, instead of being recomputed from scratch.\n  - A spatial grid means only points within the threshold of a seed are considered.\n  - After each cluster is chosen, only seeds near its members are recomputed; every other seed's cached size is still exact.\n- **CUDA:** one GPU thread block grows one seed's candidate cluster. Small and large neighbourhoods use different block sizes, and the data lives in shared memory when it fits.\n- **Speed and exactness:** the inner loop runs in single precision with a proven error bound. When two candidates are too close to call, or a candidate is near the threshold, it falls back to exact double precision and the original's tie-breaking (smallest distance, then smallest index).\n- **MPI:** seeds are split across ranks, one GPU per rank. A single reduction per round picks the winning seed, and every rank recomputes the winner locally rather than receiving it.\n- **OpenMP:** used for host-side setup and validation. Each node's CPU threads are split among its ranks, and the thread pool is started before the timer.\n\n**Things you should know**\n- **FMA:** the original binary compiles its distance and data-generation formulas into fused multiply-adds. I wrote those FMAs out explicitly, which is why results match bit for bit regardless of compiler settings.\n- **Error margin:** I checked it empirically. The largest observed error was 2.2e-7 over about 85 million samples, against a decision margin of 5e-6.\n- **Small N hangs:** both the original and the new version hang for N below about 30, because data generation never produces any points.\n- **Build machine:** CMake now requires 3.24 and builds for the GPU on the build machine by default. If you build on a node without a GPU, pass `-DCMAKE_CUDA_ARCHITECTURES` (for example `86`).\n- **Output:** only rank 0 prints, in the same format as before.
